paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is coming back, and He wants His people ready, not rattled. He says they will see the Son of Man "coming in the clouds with great power and glory" (Mark 13:26). So when the sky goes dark, it isn't the end of hope. It's the moment He shows up.

Now, the part that makes my mustache twitch: nobody knows the day. Jesus says, "No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father" (Mark 13:32). The fig tree shows how to read the signs, but the day itself stays with the Father (Mark 13:28-29, 32). So we don't guess dates, hunt for clues, or wait for a prophet's calendar; we keep the ovens ready, because being ready is our job and knowing the day is the Father's.

While we wait, Jesus says to keep watch, and that means staying faithful, not just staring at the sky. In His picture, the master leaves each servant "in charge of his own task" (Mark 13:34), so waiting well means doing your task with your eyes OPEN. And He says it to all of us: "Keep watch!" (Mark 13:37). The snooze button has beaten stronger folks than me, friend, so go do your part, stay awake, and keep your apron on.
